title: Isolated VPC: Minimal Network Binding, Offline Upgrade Safety Contract, and Air‑gapped Acceptance Tests
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Purpose: Define a minimally permissive networking and offline-upgrade acceptance contract for Private/VPC deployments that must be enforced by the operator and validated by Redwood before GA. This ticket captures the requirements, objective test cases, and operational runbooks needed to certify a customer environment as 'Offline‑Safe' (able to receive upgrades from an approved mirror) and 'Zero‑Egress Compliant' (no network connections to Redwood control plane required in normal operation). This PRD focuses on networking bindings, artifact sync/verification, upgrade choreography, observable checks, and failure-mode acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Minimal egress allowlist: A validated list of IP/CIDR and DNS entries required for initial bootstrap and optional mirror sync must be documented. For 'zero-egress' mode, the operator must be able to supply a signed artifact bundle; the product must accept an installer with no outbound connections.

AC-2: Offline upgrade contract: Customers can perform upgrades using either (a) staged mirror pull (operator-initiated) or (b) signed physical media. The platform must verify artifact signatures, checksums, and image provenance before replacing running images: verification must occur on-node or via operator tooling without contacting Redwood control plane.

AC-3: Staged canary acceptance test: When performing an upgrade in a partitioned network, the platform supports a two-tier canary: (1) single-operator-node canary, (2) 5% traffic canary across isolated nodes. Canary must automatically rollback if error rate exceeds 1% 5xxs or 10% latency regression (p50 or p95 degradation) compared to baseline within a 10 minute observation window.

AC-4: KV cache and state migration safety: Any upgrade that changes KV cache layout or on-disk state must include a reversible migration plan; the upgrade fails fast and rolls back if state migration exceeds time budget (configurable, default 30 minutes) or if checksum reconciliation fails.

AC-5: Deterministic offline acceptance tests: The operator must be able to run a bundled test suite locally that validates basic serving (health checks, end-to-end generation with test prompts, token accounting) and returns an artifacts report. The test suite must be runnable in an air-gapped environment and produce a signed report consumed by Redwood for certification.

AC-6: Observable invariants preserved: During and after upgrade, the following metrics must not regress beyond thresholds: request success rate (>99.5%), median latency (+/-10%), and token throughput (within -15%). Telemetry collection may be agent-based and sent to the operator monitoring stack; Redwood verification will accept signed snapshots of these metrics for final acceptance.

AC-7: Zero-trust networking posture: The product must operate with a default-deny policy. Any required inbound endpoints are limited to the cluster/VPC internal range; management plane interaction is optional and performed via operator-managed bastion or ephemeral tunnel. Documentation must list explicit port lists and protocols per component.

AC-8: Audit and KMS rotation during offline upgrade: The offline upgrade flow must include a KMS key rotation step that does not require external calls. If external KMS is required, the upgrade plan fails and operator is instructed to provide an offline key import file. Audit logs must capture upgrade events with signed attestations.

AC-9: Rollback determinism: Rollback must restore previous runtime images, KV cache state, and any config flags toggled during rollout. Post-rollback health checks must pass within a configurable timeout (default 5 minutes) or the operator is shown explicit recovery steps in the operator UI and runbook.

AC-10: Compatibility matrix enforcement: The installer validates node hardware/OS/kernel/driver versions against a supported matrix prior to upgrade; incompatible nodes are quarantined and excluded from automated rollouts until remediated by the operator.
testing_instructions: TI-1: Local offline acceptance: Run ./tools/offline-certify.sh --bundle <signed-bundle> in an air-gapped lab. Expected output: PASS with signed-report.json containing artifact checksums, signatures, and metric snapshots.

TI-2: Canary simulation: Use test harness to simulate 5% traffic canary for 15 minutes. Inject 0.5% synthetic errors and measure thresholds. Verify automatic rollback triggers when injected error >1%.

TI-3: Zero-egress validation: Install using 'zero-egress' mode flag. Confirm no tcp connections to external IPs during install using netstat/ss. Validate the image provenance verification step completes locally and produces the expected signature validation log.

TI-4: KV migration safety test: Perform upgrade with a large synthetic KV dataset. Validate migration completes under 30 minutes and checksum reconciliation passes. Force a checksum mismatch to confirm fail-fast and rollback behavior.

TI-5: KMS rotation test: Validate offline KMS import workflow by rotating a key using provided keyfile and confirming that encrypted artifacts decrypt on the upgraded cluster without contacting external KMS endpoints.
rollout_plan: 1) Prep: operator runs compatibility validator and offline acceptance suite; 2) Mirror sync or bundle import: operator stages artifacts to local mirror; 3) Single-node canary: apply upgrade to a control plane node; 4) 5% traffic canary across workers with metrics gating; 5) Gradual ramp with 25%/50%/100% stages if canary passes; 6) Final signed acceptance report generated and archived.
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback on gate failure; if automatic rollback fails, operator escalates to runbook steps (revert images via operator CLI, restore KV snapshot, verify health checks). Provide commands and pre-built snapshot restore helpers in the operator toolkit.
monitoring_and_observability: Must include an agent that can collect and sign metric snapshots, a local tracing collector (optional), and audit logs with sequence numbers and signatures. The console must accept operator-uploaded metric snapshots for Redwood verification. Essential metrics: request_success_rate, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_sec, cpu_gpu_utilization.
security_rationale: Air-gapped and zero-egress customers often operate in regulated environments; minimizing network surface and enabling fully offline verification reduces risk. Signed artifacts, checksum reconciliation, and KMS offline import are necessary to preserve provenance and confidentiality while enabling safe upgrades.
notes: Operator UX: provide clear failure codes and a 'dry-run' mode for the full upgrade path. Deliverables for certification: offline acceptance bundle format spec, operator test harness, signed-report schema, and runbook. Follow-up tickets should break out implementation for artifact verification tooling, offline KMS import CLI, and operator UI changes needed for signed-report upload.
